title: Ring magnet on a thread, ThinkTac (real footage)

source.credit: ThinkTac, Motion - Periodic | ThinkTac | Science Experiments, 2020

narration.transcript: Using a ruler, measure 60 cm starting from the knot on the ring magnet.

slow_motion.evidence: no captions, on-screen text or narration indicate slow motion; motion appears real-time

stated_facts.said: Using a ruler, measure 60 cm starting from the knot on the ring magnet.

observation.what_happens: A black ring magnet on a long white string swings side to side in front of a grey backdrop. It is already swinging with small amplitude at the start and continues swinging through the end of the clip.

tracking.noun: ring magnet (pointed out by Muse Spark)

calibration.note: no ruler needed: the swing is measured as an angle

pivot.why: the swing covers only 17° of arc; under 25° the path doesn't determine the radius (±47 px), so L isn't measured from it

given: string length = 60 cm (“Using a ruler, measure 60 cm starting from the knot on the ring magnet.”)
pendulum length L = 0.6 m (stated): hold L fixed and measure g
reasoning: Theta oscillates about -0.13 rad with ~0.15 rad amplitude and ~1.6 s period, matching L=0.6 m, and peaks decay slowly from 0.015 to 0.003 rad indicating light damping in air. Candidates therefore run from ideal undamped SHM to linear-damped, exact-sin, and quadratic-air-drag versions, all with L fixed and g free plus an offset for vertical.

critique.finding: It swings side to side like a big-angle pendulum with gravity {g} around a slight tilt {theta0}. It loses a little energy as it goes with damping {gamma}.
critique.headline: Ring magnet swings on, slowly losing swing to air.
critique.why_it_won: It includes gentle air damping and the true swing center so it stays matched while the undamped and textbook swings wander away.

headline: Ring magnet swings on, slowly losing swing to air.
finding: It swings side to side like a big-angle pendulum with gravity 9.826 ± 0.015 m/s² around a slight tilt -0.13024 ± 0.00058 rad. It loses a little energy as it goes with damping 0.0497 ± 0.0057 1/s.

eyeball.confidence: low - single still frame inspected, timing of 235 frames at 25 fps not available to model; values inferred from stated 0.60 m length and small-angle simple pendulum theory with typical air/pivot damping
eyeball.law_in_words: Small-angle simple pendulum period T = 2*pi*sqrt(L/g) with L=0.60 m from pivot to mass, fitted to zero-crossing times over ~9.4 s of video, with centre offset theta0 for true vertical and exponential amplitude decay exp(-gamma*t/2) for viscous damping.

clockCheck.why: Clock checked: gravity came out within 0.2% of Earth’s, so the clip plays in real time.
